**What we looked at**
We used daily prices from 2021-11-12 to 2026-11-12 (Yahoo Finance via the organizers' starter pack) and Bank of Canada USD/CAD rates. All returns are in CAD. Every past figure below describes 2021–2026 only. None of them is a forecast or a promise.

**What we found about you**
Amira, you are 26 and investing 30,000 $ for growth over 15 years. You said you would buy more after a 20% drop and could accept losing 40%. Your horizon supports that, so your risk level is 5 (Aggressive). Your loss limit is 40%, about 12,000 $. A defensive floor of 5% always stays in safer assets as a safety net. Company caps aren't fixed rules: they're worked out for you and for each asset. One company's own worst drop may cost at most 25% of your loss limit, so most companies are capped at 19.0% and NVDA at 15.8%. Crypto counts as one bet and is capped at 13.0%.

**Your request**
You made no specific request, so nothing was left out.

**The strategies, compared**
Growth tilt (most growth your limits allow): 95.0% growth, 5.0% defensive. A rule set this split (the safety net), not something the data showed. The worst-drop test alone would allow 100.0%. Main holdings: QQQ 42.0%, SPY 26.0%, MSFT 9.5%, bitcoin 6.5%. Worst historical drop -31.6%. During the 2022 sell-off (Jan-Oct) it fell -27.2%. Chance of a loss 38.1%.

Broad core (more prudent): 85.0% growth, 15.0% defensive. This is a choice offered at risk level 2 of 3, not a limit. Worst historical drop -14.8%. During the 2022 sell-off (Jan-Oct) it fell -13.5%. Chance of a loss 15.7%.

Income / dividends (most prudent): 75.0% growth, 25.0% defensive, at risk level 3 of 3. Again, this is a choice rather than a limit. Worst historical drop -10.8%. During the 2022 sell-off (Jan-Oct) it fell -8.6%. Chance of a loss 7.4%.

Over this period, all three stayed within your loss limit of 40.0%.

**Limits of this analysis and what would change the answer**
The data covers only 2021–2026, and future drops can be deeper or last longer. The chance-of-loss figures are based only on past risk. A different loss tolerance, horizon or financial situation would change your limits and these splits.

Simulation only, for a fictional persona. Not financial advice; no real transactions.
